title: Purely transcendental field extension
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. It is *purely transcendental* if there is a subset $T\subseteq K$ algebraically independent over $k$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree] such that $k(T)=K$, where $k(T)$ is the smallest intermediate field containing $T$. Equivalently, $K/k$ is isomorphic over $k$ to the field of fractions of a polynomial ring over $k$, with any set of variables, including the empty set.
